title: Several owned things: omitting minun and sinun
focus: Omit minun or sinun while retaining the ending; keep hänen in identification sentences.
targetSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
prerequisiteSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences

exercises.prompt: Write “These are your cats.” in Finnish. Begin with Nämä ovat. Address one person. Leave out sinun; keep the noun ending. Use kissa (“cat”).
exercises.explanation: Nämä ovat identifies several things. The ending -si identifies your ownership. Sinun can be omitted because the ending identifies the owner; the suffix stays.
requiredSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.targetSkill: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Nämä is the plural of tämä: several things.
Use ovat with several things, independently of how many people own them.
kissat (“cats”) loses its plural -t before -si: kissa + -si = kissasi. The ending identifies the owner, so sinun can be left out.

Correct: Nämä ovat identifies several things. The ending -si identifies your ownership. Sinun can be omitted because the ending identifies the owner; the suffix stays.
